title: A sum indexed by the subsets of [0,n+1) splits into the subsets that omit n and the subsets that contain it, and over a predicate-valued subset that split is Eq.refl
statement: For every summand F : (Nat -> Bool) -> Nat and every width n, the sum of F over all subsets of [0, n+1) equals the sum over the subsets of [0,n) plus the sum over those same subsets with n inserted. Grading by cardinality parity, the same split holds with the parity FLIPPED on the half that gains an element, so the even and odd sums satisfy a coupled pair of recurrences. Both are Eq.refl, and that is the content of the fact rather than an incidental convenience: the enumeration is a fold over the WIDTH of a Nat -> Bool predicate, so the two halves of the split are literally the two branches of the fold's own recursion. Over the alternative enumeration -- ADR-1614's Nat.Finset.decode, which reads the subset off the bits of a code k < 2^n -- the same split has to cut the code range [0, 2^(n+1)) at 2^n and then prove testBit (2^n + k) i = testBit k i below n and testBit (2^n + k) n = 1, neither of which this prelude has. A Finset-valued enumeration cannot have a refl split law at ALL, because the carrier stores a bound and decode n k and decode (succ n) k are different terms for the same set.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.Subsets.sumSubsets_succ : ((x0 : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> AxNat)) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.Subsets.sumSubsets (AxNat.succ x1) x0) (AxNat.add (AxNat.Subsets.sumSubsets x1 x0) (AxNat.Subsets.sumSubsets x1 (fun (x2 : ((x2 : AxNat) -> Bool)) => x0 (AxNat.Subsets.insertAt x1 x2))))))
formal.kernel_statement: Nat.Subsets.empty := fun _ => false; Nat.Subsets.insertAt n s := fun i => if beq i n then true else s i; Nat.Subsets.sumSubsets 0 F = F empty and sumSubsets (succ m) F = sumSubsets m F + sumSubsets m (fun s => F (insertAt m s)); Nat.Subsets.sumSel n F b is the same fold restricted to subsets of cardinality parity b (true is EVEN, and the empty set is even), with sumSel (succ m) F b = sumSel m F b + sumSel m (fun s => F (insertAt m s)) (notB b). The graded twin is Nat.Subsets.sumSel_succ : ((x0 : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> AxNat)) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : Bool) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.Subsets.sumSel (AxNat.succ x1) x0 x2) (AxNat.add (AxNat.Subsets.sumSel x1 x0 x2) (AxNat.Subsets.sumSel x1 (fun (x3 : ((x3 : AxNat) -> Bool)) => x0 (AxNat.Subsets.insertAt x1 x3)) (AxNat.Graph.notB x2)))))). The support invariant the fold maintains is Nat.Subsets.Supported s n := forall i, Le n i -> Eq Bool (s i) false, and the lemma every width-indexed summand consumes is Nat.Subsets.sumSel_congr : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> AxNat)) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : ((x2 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> AxNat)) -> ((x3 : Bool) -> ((x4 : ((x4 : ((x4 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> ((x5 : AxNat.Subsets.Supported x4 x0) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (x1 x4) (x2 x4)))) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.Subsets.sumSel x0 x1 x3) (AxNat.Subsets.sumSel x0 x2 x3)))))).

provenance.established_by: axeyum lane `inclusion-exclusion-mobius`, roadmap item W2-19: `nat_prelude/subset_sums.rs`. ADR-1624.
provenance.source: Elementary. In a classical development the split is `Finset.powerset_succ` and nobody writes it down, because the powerset of an inductive type is a library primitive.

prior_art.establishes: the same split over `Finset.powerset`, which needs the `Finset` quotient and a decidable-membership instance; this one is a fold over a `Nat -> Bool` predicate and closes by `Eq.refl`

evidence.supports: the split law and its parity-graded twin, both admitted by the trusted gate
checkers: Kernel::add_declaration (re-derives the type from the proof term)
evidence.notes: Both laws are `Eq.refl`, so what the accept/reject pairs actually pin is the ORDER and the parity flip, neither of which `refl` can supply on its own. The split law is offered at a statement with its two halves exchanged and the graded one at a statement without the `notB`, and both must be REJECTED -- `Nat.add` recurses on its right argument, so at a symbolic `n` the two orders are different terms.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: Each accept/reject test asserts BOTH directions: the theorem admitted at its own statement AND refused at the slid one. A test that only asserted the refusal would pass against a theorem that does not exist.

evidence.supports: two summands agreeing on the SUPPORTED predicates give equal graded sums -- the obligation a width-indexed summand incurs, stated rather than hidden
checkers: Kernel::add_declaration (re-derives the type from the proof term)
evidence.notes: `sumSel n F b` only ever applies `F` to predicates that are false at every index at or above `n`, so a summand built from a width (a product over [0,n), say) is free above it. This is the whole reason the width in `meetInd A n s v` can be moved independently of the fold's own width, which is what general inclusion-exclusion's induction step does.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: The hypothesis is offered at `succ n` and REFUSED. It is not a soundness question -- agreeing on more sets is a stronger hypothesis -- but a usability one, and the kernel refuses because the two statements are different terms.

evidence.supports: the fold visits every subset exactly once, in binary order, and grades the empty set as EVEN
evidence.notes: `sumSubsets 2 card = 0 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 4`, with `3` named as the answer a fold that dropped the without-n half gives and `6` as the answer a fold that visits {0,1} twice gives; `sumSubsets n (fun _ => 1) = 2^n` at n = 0,1,2,3. `sumSel 1 (fun s => if s 0 then 7 else 2) true = 2` and `... false = 7` -- these two are what the coordinated parity-flip mutant answers backwards. Widths stay at n <= 3 because every Nat numeral here is unary and the fold visits 2^n subsets.
evidence.checker_paired_negative: Every numeric assertion names the value a specific wrong formula would produce, and every Bool assertion is paired with `must NOT reduce to the other Bool`. `sumSubsets_card` is explicitly NOT one of these controls: a fold whose step read `ih F + ih F` satisfies `= pow 2 n` as well, and it is `sumSel_add` and the `sumSubsets 2 card = 4` instance that refute it.

evidence.supports: nothing of this shape existed before
evidence.notes: Pre-state measured at declarations=3000 against a binary rebuilt at this lane's base commit, with the positive control FOUND 1 and exit 0. `--name-like` returned ABSENT for sumSubsets, subsetSum, evenB, isEven, withTop and Bool.or; it returned FOUND for testBit, setUnion, prodRangeIf and countRange_union_add_inter, which is why this module builds none of those.

notes: The two enumerations of the subsets of [0,n) now in this prelude -- ADR-1614's `Nat.Finset.decode` by a bit code, and this fold by width -- are NOT related by any theorem. They range over the same 2^n subsets in the same binary order (`sumSubsets_card` pins the count and the tests pin the order at n <= 3), but no declaration says so, and the bridge would cost exactly the `testBit (2^n + k)` development this fact's statement says was avoided. That gap is recorded in ADR-1624 and is the honest limit of the claim.
